verses.commentary: And now, priests, this warning is for you. The charge shifts to direct address. Priests bear particular responsibility because they bear particular privilege. Position increases accountability.

If you do not listen, do not resolve to honor my name, I will curse your blessings. Already cursed because you have not resolved to honor me. Blessings reversed. The curse is not future threat but present reality.

Because of you I will rebuke your descendants. Dung from festival sacrifices smeared on faces. Carried off with the refuse. Graphic degradation. What priests produce becomes their doom. Ceremonial waste applied to sacred persons.
You will know I sent this warning so my covenant with Levi may continue. The warning aims at preservation, not destruction. Judgment serves covenant renewal. Discipline is love disguised.
My covenant with Levi was life and peace. I gave him these; they called for reverence. He revered me, stood in awe of my name. The original Levitical response. What was should be again.

True instruction (torah) was in his mouth, nothing false on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, turned many from sin. The ideal priest: truthful, peaceful, upright, effective in ministry.

The priest's lips should preserve knowledge. He is the Lord's messenger; people seek instruction from his mouth. Teaching function central to priesthood. Knowledge entrusted for distribution, not hoarding.

But you have turned from the way, caused many to stumble by teaching, violated the covenant with Levi. The contrast stings. What should teach truth teaches error. Leadership failure multiplies damage.

So I have made you despised and humiliated. You have not followed my ways, shown partiality in law. Public disgrace matches private failure. Partiality corrupts justice. The law applied selectively serves power, not truth.

Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us? Why be unfaithful to one another, profaning our ancestors' covenant? Theological unity should produce relational integrity. Common origin demands mutual fidelity.
Judah has been unfaithful. A detestable thing committed: marrying women who worship foreign gods. Desecrating the sanctuary the Lord loves. Intermarriage with idolaters pollutes worship.
Whoever does this, may the Lord cut him off from Jacob's tents, even if he brings offerings. No ritual compensates for fundamental unfaithfulness. Offerings cannot buy back what betrayal loses.

Another thing: you flood the altar with tears. Weeping and wailing because God no longer accepts offerings. Emotional appeal cannot substitute for obedience. Tears without transformation are manipulation.

You ask: Why? Because the Lord witnessed between you and your wife of youth. You have been unfaithful to your partner, your covenant wife. Marriage covenant violation underlies worship rejection. Horizontal unfaithfulness blocks vertical communion.

Has not God made you one? Body and spirit belong to him. What does he seek? Godly offspring. So guard yourself; do not be unfaithful to the wife of your youth. Marriage serves divine purpose. One flesh unity produces covenant children.

The man who hates and divorces his wife does violence (covers his garment with violence), says the Lord. Be on guard; do not be unfaithful. Divorce described as violent act. The covenant broken violently tears what God joined.

You have wearied the Lord with your words. How have we wearied him? By saying evildoers are good in God's eyes, he is pleased with them, or by asking: Where is the God of justice? Moral inversion and cynical doubt exhaust divine patience.
